messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 2867: gateway-5xx-surge — 5xx rate spiked to 6.2% (baseline 0.12%) across api-prod-gateway-1..4, p95 latency from 120ms -> 1.9s, scheduler.queue.depth=14_300, batcher.hol_blocks=980. Auto page sent to oncall.
megan: ack. i'm on it. seeing the same in grafana. live dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/alerts/2867
oncall-jun: taking. paging eng-runtime. starting triage. can someone paste recent logs from batcher?
raj: what customers are seeing errors? is this a region/zone thing or global?
incident-bot: Recent anomaly links: metrics://incidents/2867; affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream. Top 5xx: 502 gateway timeouts, 504 upstream timeouts, some 500s from batcher service.
megan: quick grep from batcher host batcher-03:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:01Z batcher ERROR hol_wait_ms=14200 queue_latency_ms=11800 evicted=false request_id=abcd1234 model=redwood-large-v1
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z batcher WARN kv_cache_growth=1.4x pending_batches=120 inflight_batches=256
2026-03-15T10:12:09Z gateway ERROR upstream_timeout 504 route=/v1/generate
```
megan: looks like head-of-line blocking in scheduler/batcher: large requests are preventing batch formation and causing queue to pile up.
tim: if hol is the issue we can temporarily lower scheduler.max_inflight_batches and enable aggressive eviction for stuck batches. commands:
```
# set emergency limits
rdxctl config set scheduler.max_inflight_batches=64 --env=prod
rdxctl debug scheduler evict-stalled --age=3s --target=20
```
oncall-jun: executing the eviction now. megan, please coord with ops for safe restarts if needed.
ops-bot: scheduled rolling restart of batcher on batcher-{01,02,03} in 60s window for segfault/crash safe drain. Will respect drain policy.
megan: ran the config change and eviction:
```
> rdxctl config set scheduler.max_inflight_batches=64 --env=prod
OK: config updated (effective within 10s)
> rdxctl debug scheduler evict-stalled --age=3s --target=20
Evicted 430 stalled batches; queue depth -> 7_200
```
oncall-jun: immediate improvement: 5xx rate dropping from 6.2% -> 1.1% in the last 30s, p95 latency -> 620ms. continuing to monitor.
raj: nice. do we have a fallback route to serve degraded responses for large requests? could route heavy requests to dedicated pool or apply size-based throttling.
eng-runtime: we have per-customer throttles but not enforced for some legacy keys. I'm enabling size-based fallback to dedicated-pool-ld for requests > 8k tokens.
eng-runtime: applying route change:
```
POST /internal/routing/patch
{"route": "/v1/generate", "rules": [{"if":"tokens>8000","route":"dedicated-pool-ld"}]}
```
sara: customer-success: I'm drafting outreach to top 10 customers in affected region. status: degraded for some high-throughput tenants, intermittent 504s. will send ETA ~30-60m and link to status page.
megan: after the evictions + config tweak + route fallback, stable: queue depth 2_100, hol_blocks 42, p95 230ms, 5xx 0.35%. still seeing small spikes from a handful of heavy requests. logging those ids for follow-up.
eng-runtime: probable root cause hypothesis: sudden influx of very long-context requests (some large user workloads + a runaway retry loop from gateway) caused kv-cache growth and long stall windows; scheduler allowed too many inflight batches so eviction lagged. follow-ups: add per-request size caps, improve eviction heuristics to be proportional to queue depth, patch to prevent unbounded kv cache growth.
tim: i've opened a quick fix PR to make eviction threshold dynamic: r/evict-dynamic-threshold. will validate in staging.
oncall-jun: handing primary to megan for post-incident cleanup. i'll stay on until stable for 15m. @eng-runtime please keep the patch queue prioritized.
megan: taking primary. annotating incident in tracker. current plan -> monitor 60m, validate no regressions, schedule full postmortem and customer impact table.
raj: let's keep incident open until we get 4 consecutive 1m windows at baseline. also include the request ids that caused hol in the postmortem.
customer-success: will notify customers now with a short template + link to status and assigned CS rep. escalate any enterprise customers asking for root cause to eng-runtime lead.
megan: recorded mitigation steps in incident tracker: config throttle, emergency eviction, route fallback, rolling restarts. tagging eng-runtime, infra, and cs. Will file bug for kv-cache guardrails and per-key throttles.
eng-runtime: long-term actions: (1) automatic size-based routing, (2) per-api-key circuit breakers, (3) telemetry to detect early kv_cache_growth. scheduling a two-week sprint item.
ops-bot: restart windows completed successfully on batcher-01..03 :white_check_mark:. no node crashes.
megan: marking incident as mitigated for now. keeping channel open for follow-up updates and postmortem. thanks everyone.
incident-bot: Incident 2867 updated: status=mitigated; severity=high; duration=~28m; initial_cause=HOL-blocking-from-large-requests+kv-cache-growth; actions=[eviction,config-reduction,routing-fallback,rolling-restarts]. Incident owner: megan. Link: https://incidents.redwood/2867
raj: good work. please create the postmortem doc and assign owners. close when done.
megan: will create postmortem and link to this thread. assigning follow-ups: eng-runtime (patch), infra (autoscale policies), cs (customer comms).
